item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 2 March 2023, a presidential provisional measure established Bolsa Família to replace Auxílio Brasil. It defined objectives of combating hunger, interrupting intergenerational poverty, and protecting children, adolescents, and young people through coordinated implementation, SUAS integration, social participation, and use of CadÚnico.","notes":["The excerpt identifies the act as presidential but does not name Lula; the attribution to Lula is unsupported by this excerpt."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The measure set eligibility at household per-capita income of up to R$218, retained qualifying families for up to 24 months after income increases under specified conditions, and created benefits of R$142 per household member, a minimum household amount of R$600, R$150 per eligible young child, and R$50 for eligible pregnant women, children, and adolescents.","notes":["The excerpt supports the benefit rules but does not support the stated June 2023 effective date. It is a provisional measure, not described here as a law."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The measure established CadÚnico as a public electronic registry, guaranteed interoperability with CNIS, made CNIS data accessible to CadÚnico managing bodies subject to confidentiality commitments, and was signed by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 2 March 2023.","notes":["The excerpt supports guaranteed interoperability and conditional access, but not the broader wording that it merely required or permitted World Bank policy assessment identified Brazil's fiscal and structural challenges, including an unsustainable fiscal path, tax-system distortions and compliance costs, subnational fiscal crises, unsustainable pension obligations, and underperformance in health, education, public security, and infrastructure associated partly with weak planning, monitoring, evaluation, and rigid budgets.","notes":["The excerpt supports the listed conditions but does not establish that they were inherited by Lula or link them to a particular administration."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E017","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E018","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In 2023, Minha Casa, Minha Vida returned through Provisional Measure 1.162, later converted into Law 14.620. The redesigned program emphasized housing near commerce, public facilities, and public transport; expanded eligible interventions; exempted Bolsa Família and BPC recipients in subsidized Faixa 1 housing from installments; and prioritized the listed vulnerable groups.","notes":["The excerpt supports the program's return and legislation but does not attribute the revival specifically to Lula's government."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0019-E019","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
